title: Chicago tuba players who influenced him

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What about tuba? That fellow's name that I was trying to think of last week who had recorded with Louie Armstrong was Pete Briggs.
Yeah, yeah, I know Pete Briggs. I knew him real well.
Tell me something about him?
He was a great tuba player. Really had good ideas on bass solos. I mean, he could really get over that tuba. Yeah, I remember him real well.
He was around Chicago in the late twenties, wasn't he?
Yeah.
Did he have an influence on you, you know, like you were talking about Wellman Braud, you know, being of great help to you. Was there anybody in that regard on tuba?
Yeah there was several tuba players around here then back in those days, played tuba solos, that had influence on me.
Who were they?
Well, Pete Briggs is one, that other name I recalled the other week --
Beauford.
Beauford.
Is that Beauford Collins?
His last name, I think, was Beauford. He made some records with Jelly, too, after I did.
Yes.
He was one, and then another tuba player, Mays.
Mays?
Yeah, I can't think what his first name.
Who'd he play with?
Oh, he gigged around here. All those were old-timers. Then when I started, everybody was gigging and going on. That was back in the twenties. Some of them had regular jobs, and some of them didn't.
